title: K Highest Ranked Items Within a Price Range
summary: You are given a 0-indexed 2D integer array grid of size m x n, representing a shop map.
statement: You are given a 0-indexed 2D integer array grid of size m x n, representing a shop map. The grid contains cells marked as walls (0), empty spaces (1), or items with positive integer prices. It takes 1 step to travel between adjacent grid cells. You are also given an array pricing with two integers [low, high] and a starting position start [row, col]. You are interested in items whose prices are within the range [low, high] (inclusive). You need to find the k highest-ranked items within this price range, considering the following ranking criteria in order: 1. Distance from the start (closer items have higher rank). 2. Price (lower prices have higher rank, but must be within the price range). 3. Row number (smaller row numbers have higher rank). 4. Column number (smaller column numbers have higher rank). The items should be returned in descending order of their rank. If there are fewer than k reachable items within the price range, return all of them.
constraints: Grid zero cells are walls, one cells are empty, and values above one are item prices; start is traversable.
Rank reachable in-range items by distance, then price, row, and column ascending.
Return up to k item coordinates in exact rank order without modifying grid.
hints: Breadth-first search supplies shortest distances; the remaining tie-breakers can be sorted afterward.
Traverse only positive cells from start, recording each in-range item as (distance,price,row,column).
Sort recorded tuples and return the first k coordinate pairs.
BFS distances are minimal, and tuple order exactly matches all four ranking rules.
editorial: BFS distances are minimal, and tuple order exactly matches all four ranking rules.

tests.explanation: The closest price-two item ranks first, followed by price three and the farther price-two item.
Only two reachable items have in-range prices, so both are returned.
